<reason>CON won a competitive debate by keeping the live question on the proposition’s own line: who scores “primarily spiritual” versus “overt partisan,” and at what cost. PRO’s equal-treatment and subsidy case was sharp, but its operational test kept folding pulpit naming, altar ratings, and sermon-adjacent hours into “observable conduct,” which CON used to collapse the referee/theologian distinction. PRO’s closing overclaim that a check/PAC concession decided the debate was weaker than CON’s cash-versus-worship-audit reply. History and chilling/capture weighing also landed more cleanly for CON.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>After PRO listed pulpit endorsements, altar ratings, staff time, and facilities as the stripping metric, CON turned that into a running ledger of prophecy rather than a phone-bank-in-the-narthex rule, showing the high bar still taxes naming rulers as faith.</best_rebuttal>
